text_blocks.snippet: Jardiance (empagliflozin) can cause a range of common and serious side effects because it works by helping your kidneys flush extra sugar and fluid out of your body through your urine.
snippet_highlighted_words: helping your kidneys flush extra sugar and fluid out of your body through your urine

list.snippet: Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include a burning sensation when you pee, urinating more frequently in small amounts, or cloudy/bloody urine.

Genital yeast infections: Vaginal yeast infections are common in women (causing thick white discharge, itching, or burning), and fungal or yeast infections can also affect the penis or scrotum in men.
Increased urination: You will likely need to pee more often or in larger amounts, as the drug removes excess glucose.
Increased thirst and dehydration: Losing extra fluid can lead to feeling thirsty, lightheaded, dizzy, or weak—especially when standing up.

text_blocks.snippet: Seek emergency medical attention or contact your prescriber right away if you experience signs of these severe conditions:

list.snippet: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid in the blood (which can happen even if your blood sugar is not very high). Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach-area pain, unusual fatigue, sweet- or fruity-smelling breath, and trouble breathing.

Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier's gangrene): A rare but life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin in the perineum (area between the genitals and the anus), marked by fever, malaise, severe pain, redness, or swelling in that region.
Severe urinary tract or kidney infections: Such as pyelonephritis (kidney infection) or urosepsis, presenting with high fever, chills, and lower back or flank pain.

Hypoglycemia (low blood sugar): Most common if Jardiance is taken alongside other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas. Signs include shakiness, fast heartbeat, confusion, sweating, and extreme hunger.
Lower limb amputations: Reports show an increased risk of leg or foot amputations, so you should monitor for new sores, pain, tenderness, or ulcers on your feet.
Serious allergic reactions: Symptoms include swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe hives, or difficulty breathing.
